categories.name: Qur’anic Studies
categories.description: Close readings of the Qur’anic passages cited in the Islamic Dilemma debate, in Arabic, in context and with the classical commentaries.

categories.name: Biblical Texts
categories.description: The Gospel, the New Testament and the history of the biblical text, read with Christian scholarship.

categories.name: Replies and Rejoinders
categories.description: Answers to the follow-up claims made alongside the Islamic Dilemma, about Islam, sin, salvation and the nature of God.

tags.name: Ahl al-Kitāb
tags.definition: The People of the Book: Jews and Christians, addressed in the Qur'an.

tags.name: Aḥruf
tags.definition: The modes in which the Qur'an was revealed, allowing recitation in more than one form.

tags.name: al-Zabūr
tags.definition: The revelation given to David, usually understood as the Psalms {Q 4:163}.

tags.name: Atonement
tags.definition: The Christian doctrine that Christ's death pays for the sins of others. The Qur'an teaches that no soul bears another's burden {Q 53:38}.

tags.name: Āya
tags.definition: A verse of the Qur'an; also a sign.

tags.name: Canon
tags.definition: The list of books a community accepts as scripture.

tags.name: Comma Johanneum
tags.definition: The 'three witnesses in heaven' of 1 John 5:7, absent from the early Greek manuscripts.

tags.name: Ḍaʿīf
tags.definition: Weak: a hadith with a defect in its chain or text.

tags.name: Diatessaron
tags.definition: Tatian's single Gospel woven from the four, c. 170 CE, used in the Syriac churches for centuries.

tags.name: Dīn al-ḥanīf
tags.definition: The primordial religion of pure monotheism, taught by every prophet {Q 30:30}.

tags.name: Fiṭra
tags.definition: The natural disposition God places in every human to know Him.

tags.name: Furqān
tags.definition: Criterion, that which separates truth from falsehood. Applied to the Qur'an and also to the revelation given to Moses.

tags.name: Hadith
tags.definition: A report of the words or actions of the Prophet, preserved through a chain of narrators.

tags.name: Ḥasan
tags.definition: Good: a grade just below sound.

tags.name: Ḥawāriyyūn
tags.definition: The disciples of Jesus, who declared themselves helpers in God's cause {Q 3:52}.

tags.name: Injil
tags.definition: The revelation God gave Jesus. Always singular in the Qur'an; not the four Gospels.

tags.name: Isnād
tags.definition: The chain of narrators by which a hadith is transmitted.

tags.name: Masoretic Text
tags.definition: The standard Hebrew text, fixed by Jewish scholars between about the 7th and 10th centuries.

tags.name: Muhaymin
tags.definition: Guardian, witness, trusted arbiter. The Qur'an's description of itself over the earlier books {Q 5:48}.

tags.name: Muṣaddiq
tags.definition: One who attests the truth of what came before. Used of the Qur'an, and of Jesus confirming the Torah.

tags.name: Muṣḥaf
tags.definition: A bound copy of the Qur'an.

tags.name: Nabī
tags.definition: A prophet. Muslims hold there was none between Jesus and Muhammad.

tags.name: Pericope adulterae
tags.definition: The story of the woman taken in adultery, John 7:53–8:11, absent from the earliest manuscripts.

tags.name: Peshitta
tags.definition: The Syriac Bible. Its New Testament has 22 books.

tags.name: Pseudepigraphy
tags.definition: Writing under another person's name. Most scholars think several letters in Paul's name are pseudepigraphic.

tags.name: Qira’at
tags.definition: The recognised readings of the Qur'an, each traced to the Prophet, differing in vowels, dots and a few words.

tags.name: Rajm
tags.definition: Stoning, the penalty for adultery in the Torah and in the hadith about the Jews of Medina.

tags.name: Rasūl
tags.definition: A messenger: a prophet who brings a scripture.

tags.name: Ṣaḥīḥ
tags.definition: Sound: the highest grade for a hadith. Also the title of the collections of al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

tags.name: Septuagint
tags.definition: The Greek translation of the Hebrew scriptures, begun in the 3rd century BCE.

tags.name: Shahāda
tags.definition: The testimony of faith: 'There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the messenger of God.'

tags.name: Ṣuḥuf
tags.definition: Scrolls. The Qur'an speaks of the scrolls of Abraham and Moses {Q 87:19}.

tags.name: Sūra
tags.definition: A chapter of the Qur'an. There are 114.

tags.name: Tafsīr
tags.definition: Commentary on the Qur'an. Major works include al-Ṭabarī, Ibn Kathīr and al-Rāzī.

tags.name: Taḥrīf
tags.definition: Distortion. Classically divided into distortion of wording (*lafẓ*) and of meaning (*maʿnā*).

tags.name: Taḥrīf al-lafẓ
tags.definition: Distortion of the wording of a text.

tags.name: Taḥrīf al-maʿnā
tags.definition: Distortion of the meaning, by misreading or explaining away.

tags.name: Taṣdīq
tags.definition: Confirmation: declaring true, verifying, putting right. Applied to a message or a prophet, not to a manuscript.

tags.name: Tawātur
tags.definition: Transmission by so many that collusion is impossible. The basis of the Qur'an's certain text.

tags.name: Tawḥīd
tags.definition: The oneness of God: the centre of Islam.

tags.name: Textual criticism
tags.definition: The study of manuscripts to work out what an original text said.

tags.name: Torah
tags.definition: The revelation given to Moses. Singular in the Qur'an; not a multi-book canon.

tags.name: Trinity
tags.definition: The Christian doctrine, formulated in the fourth century, that God is three persons in one being. The Qur'an rejects it {Q 4:171}.

tags.name: Uthmanic codex
tags.definition: The standard copy made under ʿUthmān around 650 CE, from which copies were sent to the major cities.
